comment: Measured heap-budget record — a ratchet, not a target. These are what the projects cost TODAY on the RV32 emulator, not what any product may use. Per project and profile mode; steady-render records only the frame window. Regenerate with `just heap-budget-baseline`; see docs/heap-budget-gate.md.

esp32c6.comment: What the FIRMWARE costs, not what a project costs: the shipped image (esp32c6,server,radio — the bytes a board is flashed with) booted whole on lp-emu:esp32c6:t1 and read from the allocator figures its own first heartbeat reports. `measured` is this tree, and is the ratchet; `silicon_reference` is a committed silicon capture and is NEVER gated — it is printed every run so the gap between the two cannot widen unseen. Regenerate `measured` with `just heap-budget-baseline-chips`; see docs/heap-budget-gate.md, "The second source".

silicon_reference.gap_note: freeBytes +8 / usedBytes -8 on our side, constant across boot 3 and boot 10, two commits, both links and both boot paths: one live 8-byte block silicon has and we do not. Sampling, boot history and the loader are all refuted; naming it needs a true power-on capture. docs/debt/emulator-heap-ledger-differs-from-silicon-by-eight-bytes.md
silicon_reference.not_a_gate: A different image at a different commit — totalBytes and stackTotal move with the tree, and comparing them across commits would be comparing two linker scripts. Read the four allocator figures and the 8 B; gate on `measured`.

esp32v3.comment: What the classic's FIRMWARE costs: the shipped image (esp32,server,float-f32 — lp-fw/fw-esp32v3's own default feature set, the bytes the DOM-Z-102 is flashed with) direct-loaded on lp-emu:esp32v3:t1 and read from its FIRST heartbeat triple. ⚠️ That triple is ELICITED, not idle-emitted: `esp32_memory_stats` runs on a project load/unload/stop-all or a client `runtime_status`, never on the five-second server heartbeat, so a classic boot with nobody talking prints no `[MEM]` line at all. The gate asks for it with lp-emu/lp-emu-validate/walks/v3-stop-all.script — the same bytes on the same trigger as lp-emu-esp32v3/tests/boot_idle.rs and as the desk sitting — and stops on the first `[JIT] used=` line. `measured` is this tree, and is the ratchet. Regenerate with `just heap-budget-baseline-chips-v3`; see docs/heap-budget-gate.md, "The second source".
esp32v3.sample: the FIRST heartbeat triple, elicited by one `stopAllProjects` on `[INIT] I/O task spawned` +1 ms; the run ends on the first `[JIT] used=` at 119,041 us of emulated time
esp32v3.stack_band_note: MEASURED ON ONE HOST ONLY, and that is a named gap for M5 P6. 16,060 B on an M2 Max at 376ebd220, twice, byte-identical; the band is that ±500 B rounded outward, which is the C6's rule (DD45's measured host-to-host spread was 128 B there) and not a fitted number. What the band exists for is that a differently laid-out image has a different deepest point: the reference image a CI runner builds is the same 2,985,952 bytes as this host's and a different sha256. Nobody has yet read this figure off a runner. P6 measures it there and either confirms the band or replaces it with the two numbers.

silicon_reference.gap_note: largestFreeBlock, totalBytes and stackTotal are EQUAL to the byte (108526 / 241552 / 45280). usedBytes is 1,156 B lower here and stackHighWater 912 B lower, and NEITHER number is attributable yet: two confounders sit on top of them. (1) The silicon capture is a SECOND boot of a flash-backed lpfs (espflash hard-resets after writing); this run direct-loads with no flash chip at all and the firmware falls back to the memory FS, which is a different allocator load. (2) It is a different build — c976f17a9 in a cold worktree, sha256 670b7bf1…, against this tree's 22ef9067… at the same 2,985,952 bytes. The same-image, same-flash comparison is M5 P6's emulated twin, and E2's pinned +84 B `[MEM] used` claim is a statement about THAT comparison, not about these two rows.
silicon_reference.not_a_gate: A different image at a different commit on a different boot shape. Read it as the two rows it is, and gate on `measured`.
